dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Owen. How can I help you?
Good morning, and thank you for taking my call. My name is Colin Sullivan. I'm calling on behalf of my mother, she lives at 37 Gidley Street, in the Fifth Ward. Thank you.
Okay. Thirty-seven Gidley. And, um, what can I do for you and your mother today, Mr. Sullivan?
Well, I'd like to make a noise complaint, if that's something you handle here. There's a rental house next to her, and they have had a loud party going until two in the morning. Thank you.
Until two in the morning. Okay. Was that last night?
Last night, yes, and the night before that as well. Honestly it has been going on since before the holidays. Weekends, and a couple of weeknights too. I appreciate your patience with me.
Alright, let me just write that down. Since before the holidays. Do you know if it's the same group of people each time?
It seems to be, yes. Young people, I believe, a lot of cars along the street. Music with a great deal of bass. My mother can feel it in the floor, she tells me. Thank you for asking.
Mm-hm. And is that the house right next door, or across the street?
Next door, on the left as you face it. It's a rental, the owner doesn't live there. I'm fairly sure of that. Thank you.

Okay. So, um, here's my question back to you. Have you or your mother called the police about it at all? Because for something happening in the middle of the night, that's usually the way it gets handled.

That's actually what I wanted to ask you. Should she be calling the police non-emergency line instead of calling here? I didn't want to tie up anything that was meant for emergencies. Thank you, I appreciate it.

Yes, yeah. For a party that's going at two a.m., the non-emergency police line is the right one. Not 911, unless there's a fight or somebody's hurt. They can send an officer out right then. We're only open business hours, so we can't do anything about it at night.
I see. Thank you. I was a little worried that she'd be told to call you, and then you'd be closed. That is the kind of runaround that has been, well, a bit tiresome.
I understand. Sorry about that. So, it would be good for her to call each time it happens, so there's a record. A pattern of calls carries more weight than one.

Yes, that makes sense. The difficulty is that my mother is somewhat reluctant. She says she doesn't want to be a bother. And, to be fair, she does have a very loud grandfather clock in the hall, so she says she's hardly one to complain about noise. Thank you.
[pause] Ha. Okay. Well, a clock chiming isn't a party till two in the morning, so I think she's fine.
That is what I told her. Thank you. It chimes on the quarter hour, so I suppose she's used to a certain amount of sound. But this is different.
Sure. Now, is there anything you want on file here? I can take down the address of the rental and note that you called, if that helps. I just can't promise what anyone does with it.
Yes, please, I would appreciate that. Thank you. The party house is the one next to 37 Gidley Street. I don't have the number for it, I'm afraid. I could find it when I'm there on Sunday.
Okay, that's fine. Let me put down next to thirty-seven Gidley, on the left. And if you get the number Sunday, call back and we'll add it.
I will do that. Would it be useful to leave a callback number? It's 401-555-0187. Thank you.
Okay, I have four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-seven. Is that right?
That is correct. Thank you very much.
Alright. So to sum up, your mother should call the police non-emergency number when it starts up, and I've got your complaint noted here. Anything else, Mr. Sullivan?
No, I think that covers it. Thank you for your help, and thank you for your time. Have a good afternoon.
You too. Take care, and tell your mother hello. Bye now.
